paper.title: SkillX: Automatically Constructing Skill Knowledge Bases for Agents
paper.central_claim: SkillX automatically builds a plug-and-play multi-level (planning/functional/atomic) skill knowledge base from a strong agent's (GLM-4.6) rollouts via iterative refinement (merge/filter/add-modify-keep) and experience-guided exploratory expansion; plugged into weaker agents it consistently improves task success and execution efficiency on AppWorld, BFCL-v3 and tau2-Bench and beats A-Mem, AWM and ExpeL.

signatures.object: skill knowledge base D = planning (S_plan) + functional (S_func) + atomic (S_atomic) skills in name/document/content/tools form; baselines = no memory, A-Mem, AWM, ExpeL
signatures.information: GLM-4.6 rollouts (4 per training task, temp 0.9) on training splits; environment feedback; tool schemas; success indicator R(tau,q) in {0,1}; current library via retrieval
signatures.operation: per iteration: roll out with current library -> extract planning/functional/atomic skills from successful trajectories -> cluster (DBSCAN cosine 0.9, up to 15 per cluster) and LLM merge/decompose -> general (LLM) and tool-schema filters -> add/modify/keep; experience-guided exploration synthesizes tasks then reruns pipeline; up to 3 refinement rounds
signatures.conditions: stop when test performance no longer improves (Eq. 8); schema-bound skills; strong extractor
signatures.feedback: trajectory success, environment feedback summaries, tool-schema validation, tool usage statistics for exploration
signatures.selection_rule: successful trajectories only; filters; merge; round count picked by test performance
signatures.selection_data: training split for extraction; test split used to choose rounds/configuration
signatures.persistence: FAISS HNSW vector store of skills (Qwen3-Embedding-8B), cosine >= 0.45, within 0.08 of best, dedup 0.95, MMR 0.75, up to 8 skills
signatures.later_use: at inference: retrieve plans for similar tasks, LLM rewrites a pseudo-plan used as retrieval query (not injected), retrieve functional/atomic skills per step, LLM self-filter, inject into system prompt
signatures.failure_boundary: over-imitation by Qwen3-32B with functional/atomic skills; limited headroom on strong models; tool-schema-bound; no retirement operation

gap.author_gap: Self-evolving agents learn in isolation, re-extract similar experience, generalize weakly from scarce training data and are capped by their own capability; existing experience forms (insights, workflows, trajectories, long-context Claude Skills) do not simultaneously offer transferability, efficient retrieval and executability.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and partly measurable (transfer to weaker models, retrieval cost), but the three limitations are asserted from the literature rather than measured, and the nearest memory methods are reproduced baselines rather than analyzed for what they fail at; the comparison to long-context Claude Skills is only conceptual (Fig 1).
gap.lineage: Voyager skill library / ExpeL / AWM / A-Mem / Claude Skills; SkillX contribution = hierarchy of plan/function/atomic skills + refinement + exploration expansion.
gap.closest_adjacent: AWM (workflow memory) and ExpeL (trajectory few-shot + insights) are run as baselines; other skill-library works (Wang et al. 2025b, Han et al. 2025, Chen et al. 2026, etc.) are cited but not compared.
gap.residue: A transferable representation of experience for weaker agents.
gap.stakes: Redundant exploration, poor transfer, high inference cost.
gap.method_response: Three-level representation, merge/filter refinement, guided exploration, selective retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Isolation of the representation's contribution from refinement/expansion and extra inference machinery; cross-domain transfer beyond tool schemas.
unresolved: Neighbor skill-library papers (cited in Sec 7) are not in the pinned inputs, so the closest-adjacent comparison cannot be verified; requested in batch notes.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C03 steps: (1) canonical schema for a task family - executed (name/document/content/tools skill schema injected into the system prompt); (2) reference substrate across categories - executed (pre-built library over apps/tools, plus exploration to widen it); (3) align query to substrate without per-task training - executed (pseudo-plan rewrite -> per-step retrieval -> self-filter); frozen base models, no weight updates; (4) hold out categories - partial (AppWorld Test Normal has a distribution gap; BFCL random split and tau2 coverage are in-distribution); (5) adversarial baseline under same budget - partial (ExpeL/AWM/A-Mem under a unified protocol, no longer-context or matched-construction baseline)
matches.success_checks: Conditioning channel is a first-class unified format; works across five base models; regime where benefit shrinks is characterized (strong models, K2).
matches.failure_checks: Test-based stopping; construction budgets unmatched; contamination/overlap not audited; benchmark-specific tool schemas.
matches.reason: SkillX adapts frozen agents purely by retrieved structured conditioning built from a reference substrate; this matches C03's retrieved-reference variant, so executes_pattern is yes, but the construction of the substrate (iterative refinement/expansion) is not part of the RS card.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Experience is partitioned by granularity (strategy order, subtask macro, tool usage) with level-specific extraction and retrieval; C04 (compression by sensitivity/redundancy) does not apply, and there is no analysis showing the levels are structurally distinct populations or an error decomposition.
matches.success_checks: Per-level behavior analysis (planning reduces steps; functional contributes most; atomic clarifies APIs).
matches.failure_checks: No uniform-vs-differentiated baseline (a flat skill list); optimal level combination differs per model.
matches.reason: Tailored treatment of differently structured experience levels is a distinct operation supporting the primary pattern.

unassigned.reason: Opus: dropped. Merge/modify/versioning is covered by H02, and there is no delete/forget policy.
sol's choice. Skills are textual tool-usage packages distilled from task rollouts, not executed parameterized callables admitted by replay; H02 fits better.

revision_proposals: H02: record 'hierarchical plan/function/atomic skills with pseudo-plan retrieval' as a variant; add 'select number of refinement rounds on a split disjoint from reporting' as a check (case only, one paper).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Retrieved structured reference skills injected as conditioning for frozen models (RS) correspond to packaged skills mined from trajectories and reused by other agents (H02).
pattern_mapping.differences: RS card stops at inference-time conditioning; the domain card covers extraction, merge, filtering and library maintenance, which carry most of SkillX's contribution.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: The H02 package is split into planning/functional/atomic levels with separate extraction and per-level use.
pattern_mapping.differences: The split is by granularity, not by source or modality; per-level gains are model-dependent.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats retained; kept on a narrower basis (shared correction). The headline rows are on the test split that also chose the iteration count and per-benchmark configuration (son55:E008, E014–E016), which is at most task under EVIDENCE rule 2. Retained rests on Vanilla-Iter1 (opus:O03), a fixed first iteration with no test-based choice that improves held-out test Avg@4.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A GLM-4.6-extracted multi-level skill library built on training splits improves weaker models on held-out test tasks (e.g., Qwen3-32B BFCL Avg@4 53.67→63.67) and leads reproduced A-Mem/AWM/ExpeL under a unified protocol.
